paragraphs: Here's what I see in this chapter, friend. Adonijah says, "I will be king!" (1 Kings 1:5), and then he goes and gets chariots, horsemen and fifty men to run ahead of him. But nobody ever handed him that throne. He grabbed for it, threw himself a feast, and had a whole crowd shouting for him, and the throne still wasn't his.

The ones who stood with David and Solomon did something different. Nathan and Bathsheba didn't panic and they didn't stay quiet. They went in and reminded the king of what he had sworn, and David answered, "I will carry out this very day exactly what I swore to you…" (1 Kings 1:30). That's the lesson: a promise made in front of the LORD is worth holding on to, and a faithful word spoken at the right time can change everything.

And look at how it ends. The man who said he'd be king bows down before the one the king chose, and Solomon says, "Go to your home." (1 Kings 1:53). I think that's a quiet lesson for us. Exalting yourself is exhausting, and it can't give you what only God and His word can give. So, baker, keep your hands open, keep your oven ready, and let the promise do the heavy lifting.
